notes: pilot_main was run twice: the first run recorded the earlier level-2 rule (tracker fission counter, 20-tick window); the rule was changed after the first analysis showed 55% of fission products are shed fragments < 50 px; the rerun reproduced level 1 and the branch counts bit for bit (max abs diff 0) and recorded the current rule.

the other arms (dt025, dt1, det, sa003, sa03) recorded the earlier level-2 rule; analyse.py recomputes level 2 for every arm from the saved level-1 series with the declared transducer (for main the recomputation matches the online record to 5e-5, float32 storage).

closure ceilings are lower bounds (linear predictor); bootstrap intervals are 16th-84th percentiles over 200 seed resamples, not ranges; the division-rate coordinate is a 50-tick window, so its short-horizon closure is inflated by window overlap.
tracker overflow: zero ticks over the caps in every arm (tracker_overflow_ticks_max).

checker.who: independent checker, core 3, about 3 CPU-minutes (rerun 27 s, tests 30 s, recompute about 2 min)
checker.verdict: The code does what it claims. The level-0 port, channel, KL check, level-1 and level-2 numbers, threshold sensitivity, overflow, CPU and next-step costs check out. A rerun of the main arm (60 ticks) and dt1 arm (40 ticks), 16 seeds each, reproduced the saved L1, L2 and ev bit for bit. Three conclusions are stronger than the evidence. (1) dt 1 'not fine': its effects are uncorrected p 0.01-0.03 among 11 statistics and do not survive Holm. (2) Level 2 'far from closed / gap is in the fields': the closure figures are lower bounds; the division-rate gap is largely window bookkeeping; the fields attribution is untested. Level-2 closure here (0.70/0.56/0.24 at 32 ticks, lower bounds) is higher than the gliders world's ceilings in EXAM.md at h >= 4 ticks (block view 0.85, 0.49, 0.14, 0.08), though a tick here is 10 time units. (3) The probe 'clears the 0.1 bar' only at h >= 20; the bar is at h <= 8, where it gives 0.04 and 0.10.
code_checks: membrane_jax.native_step follows the documented law; channel = u + sigma_a*N(0,I) on stream 0, f = (u~ @ B)/tick_time held over n_sub steps; no other randomness

level-2 rule: new slot (empty at t-1, which vw.objects guarantees is a new cell) with mass >= 50. Checker: every one of the 172 such cells in the window has tracker event 2 (fission), so births >= 50 px never occur; below 50 px there are 151 births and 214 fission products
closure: leave-one-seed-out OLS on [1, y(t), y(t-1)], oracle = within-branch variance over 8 fresh-noise replicates; reproduced to 1e-4

report_wording_not_in_summary: 'dt 0.25 costs 1.8 times as much': the pilot measured 1.59x (21.0 vs 13.2 ms per member-tick, pilot_dt025.json vs pilot_main.json)
'11-13 times cheaper than gliders': with the measured 11.4-13.2 ms and the rerun's 10.8 ms the range is 10-15x
'5 ticks, 203 nats': that is the feed arm; the starve arm of the 5-tick probe was 73 nats
'cells above 50 px grow steadily': true only above 100 px (see edit)
membrane_world.py docstring says '79-94% of [<50 px fission products] dissolve within 20 ticks'; analysis.json gives 71% (25-50 px), 91% (12-25 px), about 79% pooled
dtcheck_tick uses dt 0.125 as the reference, so first-order errors at dt 0.5 are understated by about 4/3 (observed 'order' 1.59 = log2 3 is that artefact); only 6 states
'exact paired twins': N first differs between twins after a median of 50-70 time units, so pairing adds little to the window averages (t 1000-6000); the paired tests are still valid
KL check: confirms that the channel draws N(u, sigma_a^2 I) as charged; the downstream bound rests on data processing, which this check does not test
